summary:
Zacatecas operates a legislated administrative procedure for legal gender recognition. Human Rights Watch reported on 31 March 2025 that 22 of Mexico's 32 states had legislated such a procedure, and Zacatecas is not among the six states named as lacking one.

Deputies of the 64th Legislature of Zacatecas approved a reform of the Family Code on gender identity on 23 December 2022 by 14 votes in favour to 7 against, following a positive opinion from the Justice Committee. The reform provides for issuing a new birth certificate recognising an applicant's gender identity. Human Rights Watch's March 2025 state-by-state feature records that in 2023 the director of the state Civil Registry issued guidelines implementing the law, with both entries linked to the official state gazette.

On 25 August 2021 the Congress of Zacatecas approved a ban on conversion therapies, defined in the Penal Code as ECOSIG (efforts to correct sexual orientation or gender identity), by adding fraction VI to article 182 Bis. Inciting hatred or violence on grounds of sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or promoting such practices, carries one to three years' imprisonment or up to 300 days of community work. The same session typified hate crimes motivated by sexual orientation and gender identity in the state Penal Code. A gender-identity law initiative debated alongside the constitutional and family-code reform at that time failed to obtain enough votes and remained pending; the Family Code reform passed in December 2022.
tangentialFactors: The conversion-therapy ban and hate-crime typification sit in the state Penal Code, giving Zacatecas an explicit criminal-law floor against practices aimed at changing gender identity and against identity-motivated offences. How these provisions are enforced in practice is not documented in the sources reviewed.
localsOnly:
Residents of Zacatecas can seek a new birth certificate recognising their gender identity through the administrative procedure created by the December 2022 Family Code reform, with implementing guidelines issued by the state Civil Registry director in 2023.

State Penal Code article 182 Bis, fraction VI, criminalises promoting conversion therapies or inciting hatred and violence on grounds of sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, with penalties of one to three years' imprisonment or up to 300 days of community work.
outOfScopeNotes:
The sources reviewed do not document how the gender-recognition procedure is applied in practice in Zacatecas, including processing times, refusals, or requirements placed on applicants.

Enforcement of the conversion-therapy ban and the hate-crime provisions is not sourced; no data on complaints, prosecutions or convictions under these articles was identified.

No incidents of violence against trans people specific to Zacatecas, and no data on police treatment or access to health care for trans residents of the state, were identified in the inventory.
